Verified SCOPe facts (release 2.08, current stable release; 3jb9 is the 3.6 Å cryo-EM yeast spliceosome, chain A = Pre-mRNA splicing factor 8, Prp8/Spp42, Schizosaccharomyces pombe 972h-, TaxId 284812). SCOPe cuts Prp8 chain A into five domains, from N- to C-terminus:

1. d3jb9a5 (sunid 344796), A:47-697, d.394.1.1 — class d (alpha+beta); fold d.394 'N-terminal domain of Prp8 / Spp42'; superfamily d.394.1; family d.394.1.1 (same name at every level).
2. d3jb9a4 (sunid 344795), A:698-822, a.29.2.1 — class a (all alpha); fold a.29 Bromodomain-like; superfamily a.29.2 Bromodomain; family a.29.2.1 Bromodomain.
3. d3jb9a3 (sunid 344794), A:823-1604, e.8.1.8 — class e (multi-domain alpha and beta); fold/superfamily e.8 / e.8.1 'DNA/RNA polymerases'; family e.8.1.8 'Splicing factor Prp8 RT domain'.
4. d3jb9a2 (sunid 344793), A:1605-1780, c.52.1.36 — class c (alpha/beta); fold/superfamily c.52 / c.52.1 'Restriction endonuclease-like'; family c.52.1.36 'Splicing factor Prp8 endonuclease-like domain'.
5. d3jb9a1 (sunid 344792), A:1784-2030, c.55.3.14 — class c; fold c.55 'Ribonuclease H-like motif'; superfamily c.55.3 'Ribonuclease H-like'; family c.55.3.14 'Prp8 beta-finger domain-like'.

All five domains carry the same annotation comment ('protein/RNA complex; complexed with adp, gdp, mg, zn'); none has inconsistency, repeat, heterogeneity or homology warnings in 2.08 (homology_implied_by_level = true, scope px).

What the decomposition reveals about evolutionary history. Prp8 is a mosaic: four of its five domains are placed inside pre-existing SCOPe superfamilies that were built around other, previously characterized protein groups, and SCOPe's superfamily placement is a positive assertion of probable common ancestry (not merely shared shape). The strength of the relationship differs by domain:

- Domains related to previously characterized proteins at the SUPERFAMILY level (probable common ancestry, Prp8-specific family):
  • RT-like domain d3jb9a3 (e.8.1.8) sits in the DNA/RNA polymerases superfamily e.8.1 alongside DNA polymerase I (e.8.1.1), Reverse transcriptase (e.8.1.2), T7 RNA polymerase (e.8.1.3), RNA-dependent RNA polymerases (e.8.1.4, e.8.1.6), Y-family lesion-bypass polymerases (e.8.1.7) and influenza PB1 (e.8.1.9). This is the SCOPe form of the hypothesis that the spliceosome's core protein descends from a group II intron–like reverse transcriptase / maturase lineage; SCOPe makes the ancestry claim at the superfamily level only, in a Prp8-specific family.
  • Endonuclease-like domain d3jb9a2 (c.52.1.36) sits in the Restriction endonuclease-like superfamily c.52.1 with EcoRI/EcoRV/BamHI-type type II restriction enzymes, lambda exonuclease, MutH, Vsr, Holliday junction resolvases (Endonuclease I, Hjc, RecU), XPF/Rad1/Mus81 nuclease and VRR-Nuc (c.52.1.1–c.52.1.35). Again a Prp8-only family inside a nuclease superfamily.
  • Beta-finger / RNase H-like domain d3jb9a1 (c.55.3.14) sits in the Ribonuclease H-like superfamily c.55.3 with RNase H (c.55.3.1), retroviral integrase (c.55.3.2), Mu/Tn5/Hermes transposases, DnaQ-like exonucleases, RuvC and other Holliday-junction resolvases, CAF1, PIWI C-terminal, Cas9 and Cas12a RuvC-like domains and RAG1 RNase H-like domain (c.55.3.1–c.55.3.18). Note this family (sunid 159638) was created for the earlier Prp8 crystal fragments and is reused for the cryo-EM domain.

- Domain related at the FAMILY level (closest SCOPe relationship, detectable sequence/structure similarity): the bromodomain-like region d3jb9a4 is not given a Prp8-specific family but is placed directly in the canonical Bromodomain family a.29.2.1 (the only curated family in superfamily a.29.2 besides automated matches, which also contains the human bromodomains such as d5i86a_, d5ktwa1, d4oufa_). So SCOPe treats this Prp8 segment as a bona fide member of the same family as chromatin-reader bromodomains — the strongest homology statement of the five.

- Newly observed fold: the large N-terminal domain d3jb9a5 (A:47-697, 651 residues) is the only domain for which SCOPe could not place Prp8 into any existing lineage. The fold therefore contains nothing but Prp8 — it is a fold first observed in this protein (the fold number d.394, higher than any classic SCOP 1.75 d-fold, is consistent with it having been created for the Prp8 cryo-EM structures, though I did not query older releases to verify the exact release in which it was added).

Limits (what SCOPe does not establish): superfamily membership supports common ancestry but not function — SCOPe placement does not imply that the Prp8 RT-like, endonuclease-like or RNase H-like domains are active polymerases or nucleases (the literature describes them as catalytically inactive/degenerate; that is from pretrained knowledge, not from SCOPe), and bromodomain family membership does not by itself imply acetyl-lysine binding. The lineage of a relative (e.g. HIV RT, EcoRV, RNase H) must not be transferred to Prp8 as a structural or functional template beyond the fold/superfamily level; the Prp8-specific families signal that sequence/structure divergence is large. The separate fold d.394 means SCOPe asserts no relationship for the N-terminal domain; it does not prove the domain is unrelated to anything else, and future releases could merge it if homology is found. Domain boundaries are those of this 3.6 Å cryo-EM model of the S. pombe protein (the record is in the Prp8/Spp42 protein node, not a sequence-database record); transfer to other species or structures requires their own SCOPe records. Representative selection (SPACI/AEROSPACI) and the history of the fold across releases were not queried.
